skill.name: investigating-codebases
skill.description: Investigates unfamiliar codebases by mapping structure, finding entry points, tracing imports, and documenting implementation details with file references.
skill.summary: Systematic codebase investigation for architecture, entry points, dependency paths, and feature explanations.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline file extensions, flow-diagram examples, and safe local shell redirection. The confirmed risk is guidance that may lead an agent to inspect real .env files during configuration discovery. No prompt injection attempt or data exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Limit guidance to .env.example, schema files, and config keys. Add a warning not to read real secret files unless the user explicitly approves it.

remediation.issue: Helper script examples run local filesystem inventory commands.
remediation.suggestion: State that scripts are optional and should run only on user-approved project directories. Document that they do not need network access.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger many static analyzer alerts.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as non-executing documentation and prefer tool names such as Read, Grep, and Glob when shell commands are not required.

content.value_statement: Unfamiliar repositories slow reviews, fixes, and onboarding. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured way to map code, trace behavior, and explain findings.
actual_capabilities: Maps directory structure and identifies common source, test, configuration, and documentation areas.
Finds likely entry points for Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, Java, and web projects.
Traces local import chains for JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python files.
Provides investigation checklists for architecture, data flow, dependencies, tests, and security review.
Supplies templates and flow diagram guidance for documenting code investigations.
limitations: Helper scripts inspect local files and require care around sensitive paths.
Import tracing uses regular expressions and may miss dynamic imports or framework magic.
It does not verify runtime behavior unless the agent is allowed to run project commands.
It supports investigation workflows, but it does not replace a dedicated security review.

use_cases.title: Onboard to an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Map the main folders, entry points, frameworks, and first files to read before starting work.

use_cases.title: Trace a feature implementation
use_cases.description: Follow routes, handlers, services, data access, and UI components to explain how a feature works.

use_cases.title: Prepare architecture documentation
use_cases.description: Collect file references, dependency relationships, data flow notes, and implementation summaries for technical documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Map the repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this repository at a high level. Identify the project type, main directories, entry points, and the files I should read first.

prompt_templates.title: Find a feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Find where the requested feature is implemented. Search by names, routes, and related concepts, then summarize the primary files and responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Trace an execution flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace the execution flow for this behavior from the entry point through handlers, services, data access, and response handling. Cite file paths and line numbers.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze system patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this subsystem in depth. Map dependencies, data flow, error handling, test coverage, conventions, and risks. Separate confirmed facts from assumptions.

output: The answer identifies the main route or middleware, then follows token validation, session handling, and user lookup code.
It includes related files, a short execution flow, and security notes about validation and authorization boundaries.

output_examples.input: Explain how the build process works.
output: The answer starts with build configuration and package scripts, then explains compile, bundle, asset, and output steps.
It distinguishes development and production behavior and lists the files that control each stage.

output_examples.input: Help me understand this new repository.
output: The answer summarizes project type, framework clues, top-level structure, likely entry points, and the next investigation steps.
It gives a concise reading order so the user can move from overview to implementation details.

best_practices: Start with structure and entry points before reading implementation details.
Verify each conclusion with file references and related code paths.
Avoid reading real secret files unless the user explicitly approves that scope.
anti_patterns: Do not search randomly without first forming a project map.
Do not present guesses as facts when code paths were not verified.
Do not copy sensitive configuration values into investigation notes.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps an agent understand unfamiliar repositories, locate features, trace flows, and document findings with file references.

faq.question: Does it modify source code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed for investigation and explanation, not editing or refactoring code.

faq.question: Can it run helper scripts?
faq.answer: It includes optional local helper scripts for structure mapping, entry point discovery, and import tracing when the environment permits commands.

faq.question: Which languages does it recognize best?
faq.answer: It includes clues for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, and common web frameworks.

faq.question: How should sensitive files be handled?
faq.answer: Agents should prefer examples and schemas, and should avoid reading real secret files unless the user explicitly approves the scope.

faq.question: Is this a security audit skill?
faq.answer: No. It can note security concerns during investigation, but it is not a replacement for a dedicated security review.
